events.title: Ask Me Anything about Foreign Service Family Life
events.description:
Learn about life in the Foreign Service and the latest from Brazil from a tandem couple who both serve as US diplomats.

 Ray and Jen Sudweeks are senior US diplomats currently serving at the US Embassy in Brazil, where Jen serves as Chief of Consular Operations. She previously served in the White House as Director for Immigration and Visa Security at the National Security Council. She has also led visa operations at two of the largest consular sections in the world, Embassy Beijing and Embassy New Delhi. Ray currently serves as Deputy Political Counselor in Brazil. He has long experience in Asia, having focused on North Korea for over a decade and led the team in Embassy Beijing focused on US-China bilateral relations and the Indo-Pacific region. He also served two tours in Embassy Seoul and traveled extensively through North Korea in 2011 with a delegation that won the release of a detained American citizen.

Sponsored by the Foreign Service Student Organization and the Kennedy Center for International Studies.

events.title: Devotional: Elder Joni L. Koch
events.description:
Elder Joni L. Koch was sustained as a General Authority Seventy of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on April 1, 2017. At the time of his call, he had been serving as president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission. He previously served as Second Counselor in the Africa Southeast Area Presidency and President of the Brazil Area. He currently serves in the United States Northeast Area. Elder Koch has served in numerous Church callings, including stake president, Area Seventy and president of the Mozambique Maputo Mission.

Elder Koch received a Bachelor of Science degree in statistics from BYU in 1991. He received an executive MBA from FGV/SP in 1994. During his career he has worked in senior management positions at Cargill Foods, AP Moller Maersk Group, and was the CEO of CM Ltd. at the time of his call as mission president.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu

events.title: The Buddhist Universal Monarch, Royal Nationalism, and Pluralism in Contemporary Thailand
events.description:
Joel Selway (BYU Political Science) presents new survey research on religious nationalism in Thailand. He identifies six distinct blocs among ordinary Thais and links them to voting in the 2023 election. The largest bloc strongly supports the monarchy, Buddhism, and Thai ethnicity while also endorsing respect for Muslim culture. That finding challenges the assumption that religious nationalism is always exclusionary. Selway is an associate professor of political science at BYU who studies ethnically divided societies and democratic institutions. He is the author of Coalitions of the Well-being (Cambridge University Press).

Part of the Kennedy Center's fall 2026 lecture series, "Religion, Identity, and Public Life."

Dr. Jensen, a Professor at the BYU School of Medicine, will trace the intellectually illuminating and at times challenging journey she has taken through her research into how people learn about and come to accept—or resist-evolutionary theory within a faith community. She will discuss her research findings as well as the personal insights she has gained about communicating across ideological divides. Ultimately, this journey has strengthened both her faith in God and her conviction that science and faith can serve as complementary and mutually enriching ways of seeking

The unselfish touch of Alice Louise Reynolds can still be felt at Brigham Young University. The Harold B. Lee Library can trace its beginnings to a committee on which Miss Reynolds served, first as a member and later as chair. She devoted many years to building the dream of a large and comprehensive university library at BYU. Today the Harold B. Lee Library stands as a monument to her dedication and vision.

This lecture series has been established to honor Alice Louise Reynolds and to feature women in scholarship. It is through the generosity of members of the Alice Louise Reynolds Clubs and other Friends of the Library that the endowment for this annual lectureship has been made possible.

events.description:
Anne Snyder is the editor-in-chief of Comment , a magazine of public theology for the common good and a growing ecosystem of conversation and moral imagination rooted in the Christian humanist tradition. She is also the creator and host of the Understory, Comment ’s three-day “living magazine” and cultural festival, which debuted at Washington National Cathedral in 2026.

Dr. Reich will address "Consecrate Thy Performance.” This presentation is part of the "My Journey as a Scholar of Faith" series sponsored by the BYU Faculty Center and Education in Zion Gallery.

Diane Thueson Reich is Professor of Voice at Brigham Young University and Dean of the College of Fine Arts and Communications. She received her doctoral and master's degrees in music from Indiana University and her bachelor's in music from Utah State University. A soprano, Dr. Reich has appeared in numerous recitals, concerts, and operas all over the world, playing such roles as Marguerite (Faust), Mimì (La Bohème), and Pamina (Die Zauberflöte). Dr. Reich’s students have gone on to prestigious graduate and training programs throughout the world.

events.title: The Hebrew Bible's Ancient Avengers
events.location: Hinckley Center Third Floor Lecture Hall
events.description:
Long before Spider-Man, Wonder Woman, Batman and the Guardians of the Galaxy, the Hebrew Bible’s Ancient Avengers were inspiring Americans. Ripped from the story from ancient Israel, the figures of Samson, Esther, Elijah, and David served as spiritual sustenance to freedom fighters, politicians, and pundits striving to see the United States live up to its founding ideals. In this lecture we will examine how these Hebraic heroes shaped the American story from its founding era to today.

 ABOUT THE SPEAKER 

Rabbi Dr. Stuart Halpern serves as the senior advisor to the provost as well as the deputy director and chief strategy officer of the Zahava and Moshael J. Straus Center for Torah and Western Thought at Yeshiva University. In addition to his doctorate in education, Rabbi Halpern has master’s degrees in both Bible and Psychology in Education, and an MBA in Nonprofit Management.

events.title: The Wonder of Scripture with Kimberly Matheson
events.description:
Kimberly Matheson will deliver this Wonder of Scripture lecture. She is the Laura F. Willes Research Fellow at the Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship at Brigham Young University, where she focuses on Book of Mormon theology, Christian contemplative practice, and the continental philosophy of religion. Matheson is known for authoring Helaman: A Brief Theological Introduction and for her service on the boards of the Book of Mormon Studies Association and the Latter-day Saint Theology Seminar.

The Wonder of Scripture series, sponsored by BYU’s Neal A. Maxwell Institute for Religious Scholarship, invites speakers from diverse backgrounds to explore how sacred texts shape understanding, inspire wonder, and inform meaningful lives. Each lecture offers a distinctive perspective on scripture and its enduring significance.

Elder Gerrit W. Gong currently serves as a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He previously served as a member of the Asia Area Presidency and member of the Presidency of the Seventy.

During his 20 years in Washington, D.C., he served as special assistant to the undersecretary of state at the U.S. State Department, as special assistant to the U.S. ambassador in Beijing, China, and in several positions at the Center for Strategic and International Studies in Washington, D.C. He was also assistant to the president for planning and assessment at BYU.

Elder Gong holds a doctorate in international relations and a master’s degree in philosophy from Oxford University, where he was a Rhodes scholar. He also holds a bachelor's degree in Asian and university studies from BYU.

His remarks will be broadcast live on BYUtv, BYUtv.org. Video, text, and audio are archived on speeches.byu.edu
